prerequisites: Content of the lecture "Introduction to Cryptography 1"

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have knowledge of the basic applications of asymmetric and hybrid methods.
They can decide when and which cryptographic solutions can be used to achieve certain security goals.

Students will gain an algorithmic and technical understanding for practical use through descriptions of selected practically relevant algorithms, e.g., based on elliptic curves, hash functions, digital signature methods, and Post-Quantum Cryptography.
They know how to choose security parameters for cryptographic solutions and are able to argumentatively defend a specific solution.
The lecture also prepares for courses where cryptography is used, for example in network and software security, as well as for lectures where cryptography is treated with formal methods.
Through the bilingual e-learning offering, students can acquire language skills in the academic language English.

syllabus_topics: Advanced introduction to modern applied cryptography and basics of IT security
Construction of schemes such as digital signatures and key agreement protocols
Security services (including authentication, integrity, and non-repudiation)
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the written exam. The exam duration is 120 minutes.
